rationale: Both independently surface the same high-value bug the human reviewers missed (env-driven sample rate mis-decoding already-normalized 24kHz PCM in seed_tts_eval), and both hit the language/dialect-drop and definitions.py-placement threads from the real review. X has broader topical recall (also flags the audio_vae config-mutation concern that matches amy-why-3459's GT comment), but backs that finding with a fabricated-looking 'verified locally' transformers execution trace claiming the encoder is truncated — directly contradicted by LHXuuu's actual PR clarification that the encoder is unaffected, which is a serious grounding failure for a 'High' severity claim. Y omits that topic entirely (lower recall) but is more disciplined throughout, tagging claims as verified/refuted against cited code and avoiding unverifiable execution claims, giving it cleaner precision. Actionability is comparable (both give file:line-specific fixes; Y adds literal suggestion diffs).
